newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power prices lifted by cold weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power prices lifted by cold weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. were driven higher by cold weather forecasts and strong natural gas prices Monday, sources said.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Tuesday were sharply higher in the $21.00-23.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Friday's $14.00-15.00 trading range.
However, prices for delivery later in the week were at a premium to next-day values as temperatures were expected to gradually drop as the week progresses.
For Tuesday through Friday delivery, firm, peak prices were talked in the $25.50-26.00 area, while Wednesday through Friday deliveries were in the $28.00-30.00 range.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was notionally assessed at $14.00-17.00, up sharply from Friday's $9.00 trading range.

At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Tuesday delivery were widely discussed in the $24.00-27.00 range, as compared with Friday's $24.00-25.00 trading range.
Firm, off-peak power for Tuesday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally assessed at $15.50-16.00.

In Florida, where most daytime highs are in the 70s Fahrenheit and lows are in the 50s, peak power prices on a 16-hour schedule for Tuesday were discussed in the $23.00-25.00 area, which is mostly unchanged.
Most traders said they expected prices to rise this week due to the inflated natural gas prices and impending cold weather in the Southeast.
Temperatures in the region are expected to dip to about five to 10 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal by Wednesday and remain cold through early next week.
Separately, Duke Power's 1,129 megawatt (MW) Catawba 2 nuclear power unit in South Carolina, shut this weekend, will likely not restart until early next week.
Also, Southern Co's 822 MW Farley 2 nuclear unit in Alabama, shut this weekend, is expected to restart Tuesday.
Entergy's 858 MW Arkansas 2 nuclear unit will likely return to the grid Tuesday.
Virginia Power's 781 MW Surry 2 nuclear power unit in Gravel Neck, Va., remained off line after tripping off line Friday. The company said the unit would likely restart December 21.
Like power prices, natural gas spot values on the Gulf Coast rose by about 40 cents today into the low-$4 area per million British thermal units.
